body: Most business jets stay away from wet grass strips, because a jet engine inhales air at tremendous speed and a loose stone or a splash of mud can turn a routine landing into an expensive repair. The Swiss-built Pilatus PC-24 is formally approved to do what its rivals avoid: according to Pilatus, the twinjet is certified for takeoffs and landings on grass, wet soil, dry sand, gravel and snow-covered unpaved runways. Certification came in two stages. Pilatus first obtained approval for dry sand and gravel in 2018, spent all of 2019 on a post-certification test campaign, and announced full rough-field approval in a media release dated February 7, 2020, adding grass, wet soil and snow-covered unpaved runways. European regulators approved the expanded unpaved-runway capabilities, with US approval following, and the eight-seat jet can access almost twice as many airports worldwide as competing business jets.

To earn the approval, Pilatus took the jet across two continents. Grass-runway test sites included Goodwood and Duxford in England, Kunovice in the Czech Republic and Poitiers in France, and the jet was also taken to Kuujjuaq, Canada, for snow-covered gravel. Engineers flooded an English field with about 45,000 US gallons (170,000 liters) of water to mimic rain of roughly 0.16 inches (4 mm) per hour, and in the Czech Republic crews rehearsed single-engine take-offs, engine failures and the loss of ground spoilers and anti-skid, with heavy rain adding to the challenge. Wet soil was arguably the hardest case: the Woodbridge site in England required complex conditions to be reproduced in part, just to meet every specification for take-offs and landings on wet dirt. In Canada, engineers checked whether snow packed into the flaps, whether stones reached the engines, and whether brakes and steering held up; nothing was ingested by the engines and the jet performed better than expected.

The design starts with long-stroke trailing-link landing gear that smooths out uneven ground, and main tires running at 73-76.5 psi (5-5.24 bar) so the aircraft does not sink into soft surfaces, even at a takeoff weight of up to 18,700 pounds (8,500 kg). The two Williams FJ44-4A turbofans, each producing about 3,400 pounds of thrust (15 kN), sit high on the rear fuselage, far from the stones and spray the wheels throw up, and the wing flaps shield the engines from debris. Pilatus lists a take-off distance of 3,090 feet (942 meters) and a landing distance of 2,410 feet (734 meters) over a 50-foot (15-meter) obstacle, both measured on a dry paved runway at sea level; the jet cruises at 440 knots (506 miles per hour, or 815 km per hour) and flies up to 2,000 nautical miles (2,301 miles, or 3,704 km). The capability already has buyers: Pilatus chairman Oscar Schwenk said in the 2020 announcement that the Royal Flying Doctor Service of Australia, along with operators in North America and Africa, already used rough-field runways on a regular basis, and according to a Pilatus release dated March 30, 2026, the Indonesian Ministry of Defense signed for twelve PC-24s for pilot training, air transport and liaison missions, citing the jet's ability to use short and unpaved runways as a decisive criterion. Pilatus had delivered 100 PC-24s by the end of 2020.
en.summary: The Pilatus PC-24 is one of the few business jets certified for grass, wet soil, dry sand, gravel and snow-covered unpaved runways; its approval came in two stages, with tests across England, the Czech Republic, France and Canada, and rests on long-stroke landing gear, low tire pressure and high-mounted engines.
en.title: Why the Pilatus PC-24 can land on grass runways most private jets cannot

body: 多數公務機一遇濕草地跑道就會另尋機場，因為噴射發動機高速吸氣，石子或泥漿都可能造成昂貴損傷；但瑞士皮拉圖斯PC-24已獲認證，可在草地、濕土、乾沙、礫石與積雪未鋪面跑道起降。認證分兩階段完成：2018年先取得乾沙與礫石認證，2019年全年進行認證後測試，2020年2月7日的新聞稿宣布取得完整粗糙場地認證，新增草地、濕土與積雪未鋪面跑道；歐洲監管機構批准擴大的未鋪面跑道能力，美國隨後跟進。這架8座噴射機也因此能進入比競爭對手多近一倍的機場。

為通過認證，皮拉圖斯把測試飛機帶到兩大洲：英格蘭古德伍德與達克斯福德、捷克庫諾維采與法國普瓦捷的草地跑道，以及加拿大庫朱瓦克的積雪礫石場地。工程團隊還把一處英格蘭場地灌入約45,000美制加侖（170,000公升）水，模擬每小時約0.16英寸（4毫米）的降雨；捷克的測試則演練單發動機起飛、發動機失效與地面擾流板及防滑系統失效，並遇上大雨。濕土被視為最困難的情況，英格蘭伍德布里奇場地為重現起降所需的複雜條件費了不少功夫；雪地測試則要確認積雪是否卡進襟翼、石子是否傷及發動機、煞車與轉向是否正常，結果是發動機未吸入任何異物，表現優於預期。

設計上，PC-24採用長行程拖曳式起落架，可緩衝不平地面，主輪胎壓73至76.5磅／平方英寸（5至5.24巴），讓航機不致陷入鬆軟地面；起飛重量最高18,700磅（8,500公斤），概念如同雪鞋分散重量。兩具威廉斯FJ44-4A渦扇發動機各約3,400磅推力（15千牛頓），高置於後機身，遠離輪胎捲起的石子與水花，機翼襟翼也能遮擋發動機免受碎片擊中。性能方面，皮拉圖斯公布起飛距離3,090英尺（942公尺），50英尺（15公尺）障礙物上空的落地距離2,410英尺（734公尺），均以海平面乾燥鋪面跑道量測；巡航速度440節（每小時506英里、815公里），航程最遠2,000海里（2,301英里、3,704公里）。這項能力已有實際買家：澳洲皇家飛行醫生服務與北美、非洲的業者早已定期使用粗糙場地跑道；印尼國防部則在2026年3月30日的新聞稿中簽約採購12架PC-24，用於飛行員訓練、空中運輸與聯絡任務，皮拉圖斯表示，短場與未鋪面跑道的使用能力是決定性的選擇條件。皮拉圖斯至2020年底已交付100架PC-24。
zh.summary: 皮拉圖斯PC-24是少數獲認證可在草地、濕土、乾沙、礫石與積雪未鋪面跑道起降的公務機；認證分兩階段完成，測試橫跨英格蘭、捷克、法國與加拿大，關鍵在長行程起落架、低胎壓與高置發動機。
zh.title: 皮拉圖斯PC-24為何能在草地跑道起降：從認證測試到起落架設計
